summary.headline: Q4 FY26 net profit rose 28.01% YoY to INR373.65 crore, with ROA at 2.05% and ROE at 15.03%, after absorbing a INR49.80 crore PBI charge.
summary.overview: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank reported a strong Q4 and FY26, beating every guidance figure it had given for the year, with total business up 17.37% to INR1,15,091 crore and advances up 20.32% (about 22.57% excluding a INR1,000 crore IBPC sale). Net interest income rose 24.04% to INR704.45 crore and NIM expanded to 4.18% from 4.04% QoQ, helped by surplus cash redeployed into loans and repricing of high-cost deposits. Management pulled forward the full FY26 performance-based incentive of INR49.80 crore into Q4, so normalised cost-to-income would be about 39.54% rather than the reported 44.80%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 0.73% and on-book PCR at 74.89%, but the bank faces a INR279 crore ECL transition impact from 1 April 2027 that it plans to offset with COVID-era provisions of about INR250 crore.

segments.name: Retail (mainly gold loans)
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 62.33% YoY with a 10.11% yield and 2.21% ROA per management; retail gold loans were about INR6,507 crore (vs INR6,700 crore last quarter) as customers shifted to agri gold loans. Housing sanctions rose 22% but the housing book shrank slightly QoQ.

segments.name: Agri (agri gold loans)
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 8.03% YoY, with a 2.04% ROA and 0.16% NPA. Total gold loan book is INR24,790 crore, 46.44% of advances, with portfolio LTV of 53.25%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 14.88% YoY after degrowth in Q1 FY26, with a 10.52% yield and 2.58% ROA. Management expects MSME to drive growth in FY27 and says the ROA here will moderate.

segments.name: Export credit / West Asia
segments.commentary: Exposure to West Asian countries is about 0.1% of advances (described as 10 bps); management is assessing the indirect impact of the conflict.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth to be at least 1 percentage point higher than FY26's 14.94%, with management saying around 16%.
FY27 advances growth to be defended at around 20% (FY26 was 20.32%).
FY27 ROA guided at 1.9%-2%, with MSME mix shift expected to moderate ROA.
Cost-to-income to stay below 50%, around 46%-47% over time, with branch refurbishment costs spread over FY27-FY28.
Operating profit of around INR500 crore per quarter to be defended, including Q1 FY27; NIM defended at 3.9%-4% though current level is hard to sustain.

Plans 60 branch openings in FY27 after opening 44 in FY26 against a 50 target; ECL impact of INR279 crore to be absorbed against COVID-era provisions, with a target to taper those provisions by 31 March 2027.
capex_capacity: Branch network grew from 578 to 622 with 44 openings in FY26 (15 outside Tamil Nadu); 7 more branches were in process at year end. New-branch business averaged INR40.16 crore per branch in FY26 vs INR19.57 crore in FY25.

12 CMCs (credit management centres) set up in FY26; loan management system Phase 1 is live, with Phase 2 expected in Q1 FY27. Asset resolution branches are being set up for gold, agri and MSME stress.
Technology spend up 15.80% YoY; management said spend is milestone-based and not a clean read on the year.
Manual across-counter transactions fell from 26.3 million in FY25 to 24.10 million in FY26 despite the branch expansion.
Digital transformation described as nearing completion; AI-based call centre launched and a 24/7 cyber war room in place.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth was 14.94% and CASA growth 22.35%, with current accounts up 25.62% and savings up 21.04%; management attributes this to the TBG (transaction banking) initiative and liability RMs.

Cost of deposits fell 12 bps QoQ to 5.71%, and the bank expects repricing of its roughly 8% high-cost deposits to complete by Q1 FY27, with limited immediate benefit as term deposits keep being contracted.
Advances yield fell about 6 bps QoQ; in Q&A, the advances yield was said to be down about 10 bps YoY as MSME rate cuts were passed through while consumption gold loans were priced to protect yield.
Gold loan LTV is 53.25% on net weight; the bank can absorb a 25% gold price fall, and margin calls trigger at LTV up to 90%. Gross-to-net weight difference is 9.33%.
Investment-to-NDTL ratio fell from 32% to 25%; management said a cushion will be kept and the focus is on deposits rather than redeploying investments.
Industry rate environment is hardening, with the 10-year G-sec yield up to 7.14%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank guide FY27 loan growth given West Asia war and macro risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said deposit growth should be at least 1 percentage point above FY26, around 16%, and advances growth of about 20% will be defended, with a policy of under-guiding and over-delivering.

qa_highlights.question: What drives FY27 growth beyond gold loans?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME is the main lever, growing 14.88% YoY with a 10.52% yield; car and housing loans are also expected to pick up, and housing sanctions rose 22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 agri slippage and the housing loan decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri slippage rose about INR19 crore from a single agri processing account of INR16 crore, which was classed as NPA for clean-up though it is serviced; recovery is expected in Q1 FY27. Housing loans shrank slightly QoQ, with no figure given.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the INR149.69 crore write-off and the large NPA of about INR198 crore in others?
qa_highlights.answer: Write-offs were INR66 crore in Q2 and INR83 crore in Q4 across a series of accounts, separate from the Andhra account. Cash recoveries and upgradations were INR103 crore against fresh slippages of INR85 crore. One account of INR164 crore sits in the others bucket, and a couple of cases are in NCLT.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the margin rise sharply this quarter and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash moved into higher-yielding loans and high-cost deposits were repriced. Management said the current level will be hard to sustain but believes a 3.9%-4% NIM can be defended.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gold loan LTV is principal versus interest, and what is the origination LTV?
qa_highlights.answer: The LTV uses dues including interest on the reporting date, measured against net weight. Management said origination LTV is 75%, with 80% in some cases, calculated on maturity value rather than principal.

qa_highlights.question: Can operating profit of around INR500 crore per quarter be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR500 crore of operating profit per quarter will be defended, including Q1 FY27, against Q4's reported INR522 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 ROA, ROE and cost-to-income expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA is guided at 1.9%-2%, ROE at 14%-15%, and cost-to-income below 50%, with around 46%-47% expected as refurbishment costs flow through in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How will the bank handle the gold price and the 25% sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loans are 46.44% of advances at 10.11% yield; the bank says it can absorb a 25% fall in gold prices, and asset resolution branches and margin-call processes are being set up.

risks_watch: ECL transition from 1 April 2027: INR279 crore impact to be offset against about INR250 crore of COVID-era provisions, with a target to taper those provisions by 31 March 2027.

Gold loan exposure (46.44% of advances, 10.11% yield): management says it can absorb a 25% gold price fall; watch net-weight tonnage growth (first disclosed this call) and gold price moderation, which management linked to slower gold loan growth.

NIM sustainability: management said the Q4 level of 4.18% will be very difficult to sustain, but expects to defend 3.9%-4%; deposit repricing of about 8% high-cost deposits is expected to complete by Q1 FY27 with limited near-term benefit.
MSME ramp-up and ROA dilution: MSME growth of 14.88% is expected to drive FY27, with management saying MSME ROA (2.58%) will come down; FY27 ROA guided at 1.9%-2%.

Concentration in stressed accounts: one account of INR164 crore sits in the others bucket of GNPA (about INR198 crore), with a couple of cases in NCLT; recoveries/write-backs depend on legal timelines.

Execution on FY27 targets: 60 branch openings (vs 44 against a 50 target in FY26), 16% deposit growth, about 20% advances growth, and cost-to-income of 46%-47% as refurbishment costs fall in FY27-FY28.
key_quotes: So, the NIM is at 4.18% as a consequence. And it is up sequentially from 4.04% and NIM for the overall year is at 3.98%.
And if you ask me whether this will sustain? This kind of level is going to be very difficult to sustain. But still, we believe we'll be able to defend a 3.9% to 4% NIM.
So our calculation shows that as of 31st of March '26, the change in norms from current IRAC to new ECL which, like I said, will kick on 1st of April, should have a INR279 crores impact.
We are proposing 60 branches in FY27. Hopefully, in FY27, April – sorry FY27 April when I take this call again, hopefully we should have met that.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forthright on FY26 delivery, with management repeatedly stating it beat every guidance figure and pointing to a 'under-guide, over-deliver' policy for FY27. Cautious on margin sustainability, deposit repricing timing, gold loan pricing and ECL transition, and evasive on the housing loan decline figure, LTV at origination and the gold-price-linked growth path.
